# dgbrfs

> Improves the computed solution to a real system of linear equations and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution.

<section class="intro">

Column-major LAPACK-style interface.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dgbrfs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dgbrfs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dgbrfs(
    order,
    trans,
    N, kl, ku, nrhs,
    AB, LDAB,
    AFB, LDAFB,
    IPIV, strideIPIV,
    B, LDB,
    X, LDX,
    FERR, strideFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR,
    WORK,
    IWORK
) → info: integer
```

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | in |  | one of `'row-major'`, `'column-major'` | storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | 'no-transpose' or 'transpose' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix |
| `kl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kl ≥ 0` | number of subdiagonals |
| `ku` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `ku ≥ 0` | number of superdiagonals |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand sides |
| `AB` | `Float64Array` | in | `kl + ku + 1 × N` |  | original band matrix (LDAB by N) |
| ↳ `LDAB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDAB ≥ kl + ku + 1`; row-major requires `LDAB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of AB |
| `AFB` | `Float64Array` | in | `2 * kl + ku + 1 × N` |  | factored band matrix (LDAFB by N) |
| ↳ `LDAFB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDAFB ≥ 2 * kl + ku + 1`; row-major requires `LDAFB ≥ max( 1, N )` | leading dimension of AFB |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in | `N` |  | pivot indices (0-based) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `IPIV` |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix (LDB by NRHS) |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDB ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of B |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (LDX by NRHS) |
| ↳ `LDX` | `PositiveInteger` | in |  | column-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, N )`; row-major requires `LDX ≥ max( 1, nrhs )` | leading dimension of X |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output forward error bounds |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `FERR` |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output backward error bounds |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride length for `BERR` |
| `WORK` | `(Float64Array\|null)` | out | `≥ 3 * N` |  | workspace (length >= 3*N) |
| `IWORK` | `(Int32Array\|null)` | out | `≥ N` |  | integer workspace (length >= N) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose = Transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kl`: The number of subdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KL} \ge 0$.
- `ku`: The number of superdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KU} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The original band matrix A, stored in rows 1 to `KL`+`KU`+1. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: `AB(ku+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{ku}) \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kl})$.
- `AFB`: Details of the LU factorization of the band matrix A, as computed by DGBTRF. U is stored as an upper triangular band matrix with `KL`+`KU` superdiagonals in rows 1 to `KL`+`KU`+1, and the multipliers used during the factorization are stored in rows `KL`+`KU`+2 to $2 \, \mathrm{KL}+\mathrm{KU}+1$.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices from DGBTRF; for $1 \le i \le N$, row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by DGBTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `kl + ku + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `2 * kl + ku + 1` (column-major)
- `RangeError` tenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` fourteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )` (column-major)
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, nrhs )` (row-major)
- `TypeError` if a string argument is not a valid option

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dgbrfs.ndarray(
    trans,
    N, kl, ku, nrhs,
    AB, strideAB1, strideAB2, offsetAB,
    AFB, strideAFB1, strideAFB2, offsetAFB,
    IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    X, strideX1, strideX2, offsetX,
    FERR, strideFERR, offsetFERR,
    BERR, strideBERR, offsetBERR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork,
    IWORK, strideIWork, offsetIWork
) → info: integer
```

Improves the computed solution to a real system of linear equations and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution.

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| param | type | intent | shape | constraints | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trans` | `TransposeOperation` | in |  | one of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`, `'transpose'` | 'no-transpose' or 'transpose' |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `N ≥ 0` | order of the matrix A |
| `kl` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `kl ≥ 0` | number of subdiagonals |
| `ku` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `ku ≥ 0` | number of superdiagonals |
| `nrhs` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  | requires `nrhs ≥ 0` | number of right-hand side columns |
| `AB` | `Float64Array` | in | `kl + ku + 1 × N` |  | original band matrix in band storage (KL+KU+1 by N) |
| ↳ `strideAB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of AB |
| ↳ `strideAB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of AB |
| ↳ `offsetAB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for AB |
| `AFB` | `Float64Array` | in | `2 * kl + ku + 1 × N` |  | LU-factored band matrix from dgbtrf (2*KL+KU+1 by N) |
| ↳ `strideAFB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of AFB |
| ↳ `strideAFB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of AFB |
| ↳ `offsetAFB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for AFB |
| `IPIV` | `Int32Array` | in | `N` |  | pivot indices from dgbtrf (0-based) |
| ↳ `strideIPIV` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IPIV |
| ↳ `offsetIPIV` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IPIV |
| `B` | `Float64Array` | in | `N × nrhs` |  | right-hand side matrix (N by NRHS) |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of B |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of B |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for B |
| `X` | `Float64Array` | in/out | `N × nrhs` |  | solution matrix (improved on exit) |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the first dimension of X |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride of the second dimension of X |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for X |
| `FERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output forward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideFERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for FERR |
| ↳ `offsetFERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for FERR |
| `BERR` | `Float64Array` | out | `nrhs` |  | output backward error bounds (length nrhs) |
| ↳ `strideBERR` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for BERR |
| ↳ `offsetBERR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for BERR |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | out | `≥ 3 * N` |  | workspace of length at least 3*N |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for WORK |
| `IWORK` | `Int32Array` | out | `≥ N` |  | integer workspace of length at least N |
| ↳ `strideIWork` | `integer` | in |  |  | stride for IWORK |
| ↳ `offsetIWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | in |  |  | starting index for IWORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `trans`: Specifies the form of the system of equations:

  -   `= 'N'`: $A \, X = B$     (No transpose)
  -   `= 'T'`: $A^T \, X = B$  (Transpose)
  -   `= 'C'`: $A^H \, X = B$  (Conjugate transpose = Transpose)
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `kl`: The number of subdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KL} \ge 0$.
- `ku`: The number of superdiagonals within the band of A. $\mathrm{KU} \ge 0$.
- `nrhs`: The number of right hand sides, i.e., the number of columns of the matrices B and X. $\mathrm{NRHS} \ge 0$.
- `AB`: The original band matrix A, stored in rows 1 to `KL`+`KU`+1. The j-th column of A is stored in the j-th column of the array `AB` as follows: `AB(ku+1+i-j,j) = A(i,j)` for $\max (1,j-\mathrm{ku}) \le i \le \min (n,j+\mathrm{kl})$.
- `AFB`: Details of the LU factorization of the band matrix A, as computed by DGBTRF. U is stored as an upper triangular band matrix with `KL`+`KU` superdiagonals in rows 1 to `KL`+`KU`+1, and the multipliers used during the factorization are stored in rows `KL`+`KU`+2 to $2 \, \mathrm{KL}+\mathrm{KU}+1$.
- `IPIV`: The pivot indices from DGBTRF; for $1 \le i \le N$, row i of the matrix was interchanged with row `IPIV(i)`.
- `B`: The right hand side matrix B.
- `X`: On entry, the solution matrix X, as computed by DGBTRS. On exit, the improved solution matrix X.
- `FERR`: The estimated forward error bound for each solution vector `X(j)` (the j-th column of the solution matrix X). If XTRUE is the true solution corresponding to `X(j)`, `FERR(j)` is an estimated upper bound for the magnitude of the largest element in (`X(j)` - XTRUE) divided by the magnitude of the largest element in `X(j)`. The estimate is as reliable as the estimate for RCOND, and is almost always a slight overestimate of the true error.
- `BERR`: The componentwise relative backward error of each solution vector `X(j)` (i.e., the smallest relative change in any element of A or B that makes `X(j)` an exact solution).

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 if successful

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid transpose operation
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` `IWORK` must have at least `N` elements from `offsetIWork`

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Int32Array from '@stdlib/array/int32/lib/index.js';
import dgbtrf from './../../dgbtrf/lib/base.js';
import dgbtrs from './../../dgbtrs/lib/base.js';
import dgbrfs from './../lib/base.js';

// 1x1 system: 3*x = 5
const ab = new Float64Array( [ 3.0 ] );

const afb = new Float64Array( [ 3.0 ] );

const ipiv = new Int32Array( 1 );
dgbtrf( 1, 1, 0, 0, afb, 1, 1, 0, ipiv, 1, 0 );

const b = new Float64Array( [ 5.0 ] );

const x = new Float64Array( 1 );
x[ 0 ] = b[ 0 ];
dgbtrs( 'no-transpose', 1, 0, 0, 1, afb, 1, 1, 0, ipiv, 1, 0, x, 1, 1, 0 );

const ferr = new Float64Array( 1 );
const berr = new Float64Array( 1 );
const work = new Float64Array( 3 );
const iwork = new Int32Array( 1 );

const info = dgbrfs( 'no-transpose', 1, 0, 0, 1, ab, 1, 1, 0, afb, 1, 1, 0, ipiv, 1, 0, b, 1, 1, 0, x, 1, 1, 0, ferr, 1, 0, berr, 1, 0, work, 1, 0, iwork, 1, 0 ); // eslint-disable-line max-len

console.log( 'info: %d', info );
console.log( 'x: %d', x[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'ferr: %d', ferr[ 0 ] );
console.log( 'berr: %d', berr[ 0 ] );
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGBRFS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGBRFS improves the computed solution to a system of linear equations when the coefficient matrix is banded, and provides error bounds and backward error estimates for the solution.

</section>
